bib.title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation", Junnan Li, Dongxu Li, Caiming Xiong, Steven Hoi (Salesforce Research). The PDF names no venue. It is stamped "arXiv:2201.12086v2 [cs.CV] 15 Feb 2022", so cite it as a preprint, 2022. The PDF does not state the ICML 2022 venue, and I did not use it.

COVERAGE: I read all 51,990 of 51,990 chars: the body, Tables 1–15, Appendices A–C (finetuning details, the Figure 6 examples, dataset statistics) and every reference. Nothing was skipped. I also pulled the figure captions with figures.py.

CLAIMS
- claim: CapFilt (captioner plus filter, applied together) improves every downstream metric over training on the raw web text, at the same 14M images and ViT-B/16 backbone.
  number: COCO-FT TR@1 78.4→80.6, IR@1 60.7→63.1; Flickr-ZS TR@1 93.9→94.8, IR@1 82.1→84.9; COCO caption CIDEr 127.8→129.7; NoCaps-ZS CIDEr 102.2→105.1
  setup: Pre-trained on COCO+VG+CC+SBU (14M images), ViT-B/16, with a ViT-B captioner and filter. Retrieval is finetuned on COCO and zero-shot on Flickr. Captioning is finetuned on COCO and zero-shot on NoCaps.
  quote: Table 1 rows "78.4 60.7 93.9 82.1 38.0 127.8 102.2 13.9" (no bootstrap) and "B B 80.6 63.1 94.8 84.9 38.6 129.7 105.1 14.4"
  where: p5 (Table 1), chars ~22,000
- claim: The captioner alone and the filter alone each help, and the two effects add up. The extraction drops the checkmarks, so you cannot tell which single-module row is which (see PROBLEMS).
  number: single-module rows give TR@1 79.1 / 79.7 and NoCaps CIDEr 102.7 / 103.4
  setup: 14M images, ViT-B
  quote: "  B 79.1 61.5 94.1 82.8 38.1 128.2 102.7 14.0" / "B  79.7 62.0 94.4 83.6 38.4 128.9 103.4 14.2"; text: "When only the captioner or the filter is applied to the dataset with 14M images, performance improvement can be observed. When applied together, their effects compliment each other"
  where: p5 (Table 1 and Section 4.2)
- claim: CapFilt still helps at 129M images, when LAION's 115M images are added. A ViT-L captioner and filter also improve a ViT-B student.
  number: 129M with no bootstrap: TR@1 79.6, CIDEr 130.1, NoCaps 105.4. With ViT-B CapFilt: 81.9 / 131.4 / 106.3. With ViT-L CapFilt (ViT-B student): 81.2 / 133.3 / 109.6
  setup: COCO+VG+CC+SBU+LAION (129M images), ViT-B/16 student
  quote: "79.6 62.0 94.3 83.6 38.8 130.1 105.4 14.2", "B B 81.9 64.3 96.0 85.0 39.4 131.4 106.3 14.3", "L L 81.2 64.1 96.0 85.5 39.7 133.3 109.6 14.7"
  where: p5 (Table 1)
- claim: Nucleus sampling gives better synthetic captions than beam search, even though the filter flags more of them as noisy. The authors put this down to diversity: beam search produces "safe captions that are common in the dataset."
  number: noise ratio 19% for beam vs 25% for nucleus; TR@1 79.6 vs 80.6; NoCaps CIDEr 103.5 vs 105.1; nucleus uses p = 0.9
  setup: 14M images, one synthetic caption per image
  quote: "Beam 19% 79.6 61.9 94.1 83.1 38.4 128.9 103.5 14.2 / Nucleus 25% 80.6 63.1 94.8 84.9 38.6 129.7 105.1 14.4"; "(p = 0.9 in our experiments)"; "Nucleus sampling leads to evidently better performance, despite being more noisy as suggested by a higher noise ratio from the filter."
  where: p5–6 (Table 2, Section 4.3)
- claim: The captioner and filter must be finetuned separately. When they share parameters, the filter passes the captioner's own noisy captions ("confirmation bias") and downstream scores drop.
  number: noise ratio 8% when shared vs 25% when decoupled; TR@1 79.8 vs 80.6
  setup: 14M images
  quote: "Share parameters 8% 79.8 62.2 94.3 83.7 38.4 129.0 103.5 14.2 / Decoupled 25% 80.6 63.1 94.8 84.9 38.6 129.7 105.1 14.4"; "as indicated by the lower noise ratio (8% compared to 25%)"
  where: p6 (Table 4)
- claim: The gain is not explained by longer training. Copying the web texts up to the bootstrapped dataset's size does not help.
  number: 15.3M texts without CapFilt: TR@1 78.4. 24.7M replicated texts without CapFilt: 78.3. 24.7M texts with CapFilt: 80.6
  setup: 14M images
  quote: "No 15.3M 78.4 ... No 24.7M 78.3 ... Yes 24.7M 80.6 63.1 94.8 84.9 38.6 129.7 105.1 14.4"
  where: p9 (Table 12)
- claim: The bootstrapped data should train a fresh model. Continuing training from the old checkpoint does not help, which the authors liken to knowledge distillation, where the student is not initialised from the teacher.
  number: continued training: NoCaps CIDEr 104.5; fresh model: 105.1
  setup: 14M images
  quote: "Yes 80.6 63.0 94.5 84.6 38.5 129.9 104.5 14.2 / No 80.6 63.1 94.8 84.9 38.6 129.7 105.1 14.4"

- claim: MED is one model with three modes: a unimodal encoder trained with ITC, an image-grounded text encoder that adds cross-attention and is trained with ITM, and an image-grounded decoder that uses causal self-attention and is trained with LM. The encoder and decoder share every parameter except the self-attention layers. Each pair needs one ViT pass and three text-transformer passes.
  number: sharing all layers except SA gives 252M parameters and TR@1 78.4. Sharing all layers gives 224M and 77.3. Sharing none gives 361M and 78.3

  quote: "All 224M 77.3 ... All except SA 252M 78.4 60.7 ... None 361M 78.3"; "the text encoder and text decoder share all parameters except for the SA layers"
  where: p3 (Section 3.1–3.2), p5 (Table 3)
- claim: Headline retrieval: on the same 14M images, BLIP beats ALBEF on COCO.
  number: "+2.7% in average recall@1"; COCO TR@1 80.6 vs 77.6 and IR@1 63.1 vs 60.7. The best result is ViT-L at 129M: TR@1 82.4, IR@1 65.1
  setup: Finetuned on COCO, 5K test set. Candidates are picked by feature similarity and reranked by ITM, with k=256 for COCO and k=128 for Flickr
  quote: "BLIP outperforms the previous best model ALBEF by +2.7% in average recall@1 on COCO"; "BLIPViT-L 129M 82.4 95.4 97.9 65.1"

- claim: Zero-shot Flickr30K retrieval, using the model finetuned on COCO.
  number: BLIP 14M: TR@1 94.8 / IR@1 84.9. ViT-L: 96.7 / 86.7. CLIP (400M images): 88.0 / 68.7
  setup: Flickr30K 1K test set
  quote: "BLIP 14M 94.8 99.7 100.0 84.9"; "CLIP 400M 88.0 98.7 99.4 68.7"
  where: p6 (Table 6)
- claim: Captioning: BLIP ViT-L at 129M images roughly matches LEMON-large at 200M, without an object detector and at 384×384 input instead of 800×1333.
  number: NoCaps overall CIDEr 113.2 vs 113.4; COCO CIDEr 136.7 vs 135.7. SimVLM-huge (1.8B images) reaches COCO CIDEr 143.3
  setup: Finetuned on COCO Karpathy with cross-entropy loss and the prompt "a picture of". Beam size 3, max length 20
  quote: "BLIPViT-L 129M 114.9 15.2 112.1 14.9 115.3 14.4 113.2 14.8 40.4 136.7"; "LEMONlarge† ... 200M ... 113.4 15.0 40.6 135.7"
  where: p7 (Table 7), Appendix A
- claim: VQA is framed as answer generation. At inference the decoder ranks 3,128 candidate answers. BLIP beats ALBEF at 14M images, and at 129M it beats SimVLM-base, which used 1.8B images.
  number: test-std 77.62 at 14M vs ALBEF 76.04. At 129M: 78.17 (78.32 with CapFilt-L) vs SimVLM-base 78.14
  setup: VQA2.0 with train+val plus VG, 480×480 images
  quote: "BLIP 14M 77.54 77.62"; "ALBEF 14M 75.84 76.04"; "SimVLMbase† 1.8B 77.87 78.14"; "BLIPCapFilt-L 129M 78.25 78.32"
  where: p7 (Table 8), Appendix A
- claim: Zero-shot transfer to video works even though temporal order is ignored (frames are simply concatenated). Zero-shot BLIP beats finetuned video models on MSRVTT retrieval.
  number: R@1 43.3 zero-shot vs 30.9 for finetuned VideoCLIP ("+12.4%")
  setup: MSRVTT 1k test, 8 frames per video, model finetuned on COCO retrieval
  quote: "BLIP 43.3 65.6 74.7 2"; "zero-shot BLIP even outperforms models finetuned on the target video dataset by +12.4% in recall@1"
  where: p8 (Table 10)
- claim: Compute and recipe. Pre-training ran on two 16-GPU nodes for 20 epochs, initialised from an ImageNet ViT and BERT-base.
  number: batch size 2880 (ViT-B) / 2400 (ViT-L); LR 3e-4 / 2e-4; images 224² in pre-training and 384² in finetuning
  setup: Section 4.1. No GPU type or wall-clock time is given
  quote: "pre-trained on two 16-GPU nodes"; "We pre-train the model for 20 epochs using a batch size of 2880 (ViT-B) / 2400 (ViT-L)"

- claim: Pre-training data sizes.
  number: 14M images (COCO 113K, VG 100K, SBU 860K, CC3M 3M, CC12M 10M) plus LAION 115M, giving 129M. Only 1/5 of LAION is used per epoch
  setup: Table 15, footnote 1

LIMITS
- NLVR2 gains little from extra web images. The authors say this is "possibly due to the domain gap", and ALBEF beats them on NLVR2 test-P (83.14 vs 82.30 at 14M).
- The video results ignore temporal information.
- Only one synthetic caption is made per image, and bootstrapping runs only once. The conclusion lists multiple rounds, multiple captions and captioner/filter ensembles as future work.
- No compute or wall-clock cost is reported for CapFilt itself. Running the captioner and filter over 129M images goes unmeasured.
- The filter's "noise ratio" is the filter's own verdict, not a human audit. No human check of caption quality is reported.
- The authors give no error bars or seed variance. Many gains are 0.5–2 points.
- The captioner and filter are finetuned on COCO, which is also the evaluation domain, so some of the gain may be COCO-style captions leaking in. The paper does not test this.
- SNLI-VE is omitted because its test data is noisy.
- What has dated: this is the 2022 state of the art with BERT-base text towers. The SimVLM-huge comparison (COCO CIDEr 143.3) already exceeds BLIP.

BUILDS ON: ALBEF (Li et al., 2021a): ITC with a momentum encoder and soft labels, ITM hard-negative mining, the 14M dataset, retrieval rerank, and VQA as generation. Also ViT (Dosovitskiy et al., 2021), BERT (Devlin et al., 2019), nucleus sampling (Holtzman et al., 2020), knowledge distillation (Hinton et al., 2015), noisy-student self-training (Xie et al., 2020), CLIP (Radford et al., 2021), SimVLM (Wang et al., 2021) for the "a picture of" prompt and 480px VQA, the unified VLP encoder-decoder (Zhou et al., 2020), UNITER (Chen et al., 2020), LAION-400M (Schuhmann et al., 2021) and Conceptual Captions/CC12M (Sharma et al., 2018; Changpinyo et al., 2021).

CODE: The paper contains no code snippets. The repo link printed on p1 is https://github.com/salesforce/BLIP

FIGURES
- Fig 2, p2: "Pre-training model architecture and objectives of BLIP (same parameters have the same color)". One picture shows the three MED modes and their losses (ITC, ITM, LM) and which layers are shared. This is faster than the prose for "What the model actually sees".
- Fig 3, p4: "Learning framework of BLIP. We introduce a captioner to produce synthetic captions for web images, and a filter to remove noisy image-text pairs." The full CapFilt loop (pre-train → finetune Cap/Filt on COCO → bootstrap → pre-train new model) on one page. Best fit for the data-quality section.
- Fig 4, p5 and Fig 6, p12: "Examples of the web text Tw and the synthetic text Ts. Green texts are accepted by the filter, whereas red texts are rejected." Concrete alt-text noise, e.g. "the current castle was built in 1180..." vs "a large building with a lot of windows on it".
- Fig 1, p1: a minimal Cap/Filt cartoon.

PROBLEMS
- In Table 1 the C/F checkmark columns came out of extraction as spaces or "B". The rows "  B 79.1..." and "B  79.7..." are each a single module, but I cannot tell which is captioner-only and which is filter-only. Check the PDF page 5 visually before attributing them.
- Table 1's last two rows are merged ("ViT-L/16 80.6 64.1 95.1 85.5 40.3 135.5 112.5 14.7L L 82.4 ..."). Read as: ViT-L backbone with no bootstrap gives 80.6/64.1/95.1/85.5/40.3/135.5/112.5/14.7, and with an L/L CapFilt gives 82.4/65.1/96.7/86.7/40.4/136.7/113.2/14.8.
- Figure-internal text (diagram labels, LaTeX symbols such as 𝑇!, 𝑇") is garbled but not needed.
- The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
